src.q: Febuxostat is a 2-arylthiazole derivative that achieves its therapeutic effect of decreasing serum uric acid by selectively inhibiting XO
It acts by direct stimulation of the D2-dopamine receptors on pituitary lactotrophs, thus inhibiting PRL secretion.
Cabergoline is a dopaminergic ergoline derivative endowed with a potent and long-lasting PRL-lowering activity.

conditions.name: Acute illness with fluid or electrolyte imbalance (e.g. systemic infection, fever, gastroenteritis)
Severe bladder dysfunction or bladder outlet obstruction
History of pulmonary, pericardial or retroperitoneal fibrotic disorder
Unhealed open soft-tissue lesions in the mouth (e.g. after dental or oral surgery)
Han Chinese, Thai or Korean ancestry (high HLA-B*5801 prevalence)
Acute gout attack (flare) not yet settled
Greatly increased urate formation (e.g. malignancy and its treatment, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome)

notes: BATCH AD (desmopressin, cabergoline, tamsulosin, denosumab, allopurinol, febuxostat). All six have UK product information; none is no-uk-product. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). (1) DESMOPRESSIN: the clinic brand (120 microgram melt) is not on emc; two UK SmPCs of the same form/strength are used: emc-102061 (sublingual lyophilisate; DI, post-hypophysectomy polyuria, PNE) and emc-14771 (oral lyophilisate; PNE only). The 4.3 list (normal BP only, not over 65, CrCl below 50 ml/min, known hyponatraemia, SIADH) is headed "related to the treatment of primary nocturnal enuresis" in emc-102061; for DI only cardiac insufficiency/diuretic-requiring conditions, psychogenic polydipsia and alcohol abuse apply. The engine cannot filter by indication, so these rules fire for every use; the concern text says "nocturnal enuresis use". The 4.3 phrase "conditions requiring treatment with diuretic agents" is encoded as an interaction rule with group:diuretic (contraindicated). Sulfonylurea interaction kept at info because the SmPC says only "some" sulfonylureas, particularly chlorpropamide (not in master list). Noqdirna (25/50 microgram, nocturia) and older DDAVP Melt SmPCs were not used. No BUMPS leaflet or SPS breastfeeding page found. (2) CABERGOLINE: SmPC 4.3 contraindicates "hepatic insufficiency" (no grade) while 4.4 advises considering lower doses in severe hepatic insufficiency on prolonged treatment; both kept (contraindicated any + dose severe). 4.3 antipsychotic co-administration: no antipsychotic in the master list, so text only. Dopamine antagonists mapped to group:dopamine-antagonist (members domperidone, metoclopramide from other batches) because the SmPC names "drugs which have dopamine-antagonist activity" including metoclopramide. Valvulopathy contraindication is for long-term treatment only (rule concern says so). New groups dopamine-agonist and ergot-derivative (member cabergoline) added for allergy cross-reactivity. (3) TAMSULOSIN: clinic product is 0.4 mg tablets; the UK prolonged-release 400 microgram tablet SmPC (emc-97) is used. The "should not be given with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in CYP2D6 poor metabolisers" statement cannot be encoded (genotype + drug); kept in the action text of the caution rule. Pregnancy: SmPC says not indicated in women; BUMPS says generally avoided; rule level avoid. (4) DENOSUMAB: 60 mg product only. Severe renal impairment threshold is CrCl below 30 mL/min (SmPC + MHRA 2014); MHRA 2012 also gives eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73m2 as equivalent - CrCl used. SmPC 4.2 separately mentions GFR below 30 mL/min (no data with long-term glucocorticoids) - text only. Glucocorticoids are an additional hypocalcaemia risk factor in 4.4; not mapped to prednisolone/dexamethasone rules because the SmPC names only "glucocorticoid treatment" (text only; integrator may decide). MHRA 2020 advice (do not stop without specialist review; multiple vertebral fractures within 18 months of stopping/delaying) is in restrictions, cautions, monitoring and counselling. No newer MHRA CKD-hypocalcaemia article found on GOV.UK. No BUMPS leaflet. (5) ALLOPURINOL: UK SmPCs (Zyloric and generics checked on emc) give NO CrCl/eGFR dose bands - only "severe renal insufficiency: less than 100 mg/day or 100 mg at longer intervals" and a dialysis schedule. So renal advice is encoded as condition rules (renal-impairment, severe-renal-impairment, end-stage-renal-disease) not numeric renal rules. The oral-suspension SmPC (emc-101982, not used) cites a literature proposal of 50 mg every 2 days for eGFR 16-30 and refers to UK national guidance (max initial 100 mg daily); not used as a rule. Azathioprine/mercaptopurine (avoid; if needed give 25% dose) are not in the master list: text only. Amoxicillin interaction also applied to co-amoxiclav (contains amoxicillin). CONFLICT: pregnancy - SmPC "use only when there is no safer alternative" vs BUMPS "can be used in pregnancy if recommended by a specialist"; both shown, rule level caution. Breastfeeding: SmPC not recommended; no SPS page found. (6) FEBUXOSTAT: MHRA May 2023 (replacing July 2019 "avoid" advice) says use cautiously in pre-existing major CV disease; encoded as caution rules on ischaemic-heart-disease, cerebrovascular-disease, unstable-angina, with NICE NG219 "offer allopurinol first line" in the action. MHRA 2012: prior allopurinol hypersensitivity may indicate potential febuxostat hypersensitivity -> allergy rule (caution) with allergen allopurinol. Mercaptopurine/azathioprine (not recommended; 20% dose if unavoidable) not in master list: text only. No master-list interaction needs a rule (NSAIDs, warfarin, hydrochlorothiazide, antacids: no adjustment per SmPC). Severe renal (CrCl below 30 mL/min) and severe hepatic impairment are "not studied" -> info rules. No BUMPS leaflet. No UK source found stating brand-name prescribing for any of the six. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second check, see audit/AD-AE.md): desmopressin hyponatraemia and SIADH contraindications now say 'nocturnal enuresis use' (emc-102061 lists them only under the enuresis heading); renal CrCl<50 kept as a blanket contraindication because 4.2 and 5.2 state it without an indication, with the 4.3 heading noted in the consequence; desmopressin adverseCommon corrected from the HTML 4.8 table (only headache is common; GI effects are uncommon). Tamsulosin moderate-CYP3A4 rule now has otherExcept clarithromycin (it has its own strong-inhibitor rule). Allopurinol 'large doses of salicylate' rule limited to otherFormulations aspirin-analgesic (no longer fires for 75 mg aspirin). Denosumab: new monitor rule with group:corticosteroid (SmPC 4.4: concomitant glucocorticoid treatment is an additional risk factor for hypocalcaemia; corticosteroid group = oral prednisolone and dexamethasone only). Licence checks: all six UK SmPCs are on emc as current products.
